summary: Flown, this config lands softly from every band at every load and never finds a reason to skim — the cheapest descent is always a single committed pass, ascent fails outright at all three bands, and the params' heat-index and pass-count claims are contradicted by the simulator.

findings.claim: game_params flight (dry_mass_kg 1200, fuel_capacity_kg 620, thrust_n 16000, fuel_burn_kgs 4) is asserted to deliver 1666 m/s of delta-v at launch TWR 2.2, enough to circularise suborbital at ~1350 m/s with ~315 m/s spare, with the low band reachable at base 'with no margin'.
findings.measured: The verification sweep flew all three ascents and all three read reached=false, why='crashed on ascent', fuel_remaining_kg 0, fuel_margin_pct 0 — suborbital (102500 m), low (170000 m) and high (275000 m) alike. Zero of three bands are reachable as configured, against a design that needs at least two. In the exploration grid bands_reachable is satisfied by 57.7% of the 324 worlds and fuel_margin_sane by 32.7%, so the space of working ascents is large and this is a wrong-numbers problem, not an impossible one.

findings.claim: GDD 2.3.1 requires the cheapest descent to be 2-4 committed passes, never a single plunge and never feathering; game_params.ablation.optimal_skims asserts 0/1/2 for suborbital/low/high with cost curves showing a genuine interior minimum at low (20.85 -> 20.41) and high (39.33 -> 37.33 -> 36.54).
findings.measured: Every one of the nine flown descents reports cheapest_pass_count = 1. The measured ablation curve is monotonically increasing in pass count with no interior minimum anywhere: suborbital full hold 10.0 / 11.6 / 12.4 / 13.0 / 13.6 / 14.2 / 14.8; low full hold 8.7 / 11.1 / 12.1 / 12.8 / 13.4; high full hold 7.7 / 11.3 / 12.3 / 13.0 / 13.8. The second pass costs 1.6-3.6 points of plate and buys nothing. The params' claimed high-band curve (39.33 / 37.33 / 36.54) is contradicted both in shape and in absolute level — the simulator's high-band figures are 7.7-13.0%, roughly a fifth of the claim.

findings.claim: Aerobraking is described as essential from high orbits and ablation.skim_heat_multiplier [1.0, 0.971, 0.944, 0.918] is adopted as the flown high-band array, with optimal_skims 2 at high.
findings.measured: At the shallowest entry depth the measured multipliers are high [1, 0.971, 0.944, 0.918], low [1, 0.956, 0.912, 0.867], suborbital [1, 0.898, 0.730, 0.730]. Two skims from the high band remove 5.6% of peak heat (157.1 -> 148.4) and cost 47 m/s of commit burn plus 1.8 extra hours of orbit time. Entry depth is 5-10x the stronger lever over the same range: high band 157.1 at depth 0 versus 100.6 at depth 39000, a 36% reduction from one choice. Skimming is therefore real but negligible, and the design's central descent decision is being made by a variable the params do not expose. Across the grid skimming_cools_the_entry is satisfiable in 43.8% of worlds, so a stronger skim exists — every grid config that gets it (multipliers down to 0.262-0.363) does so at ballistic_coefficient_staged 44.4, below the ~50 kg/m2 floor where the atmosphere stops the ship instead of braking it.

findings.claim: ablation.heat_index 100 / 126.6 / 157.1 is anchored to an empty single-pass suborbital descent = 100, and the balance notes conclude a base-gear direct suborbital entry 'sits on the cargo-damage line', the low band 'requires heat_shield t1' and the high band 'requires t2'.
findings.measured: The heat-index numbers are reproduced exactly by the skim sweep (suborbital 100, low 126.6, high 157.1 at entry_depth 0), so the normalisation is honest. But those are the shallowest-entry figures, and the flown descents choose their own braking altitude: measured peak heat for a single-pass descent is 70 (suborbital empty), 98 (suborbital full), 67 / 93 (low), 64 / 89 (high). Every flown descent peaks below reentry.heat_capacity 100 at base gear, and plate_survives is true in all nine. The upgrade gating the params derive from heat_index does not exist in flight — nothing forces heat_shield t1 or t2, and the high band is the coolest single-pass entry in the set (64 empty) because a deeper committed entry brakes earlier.

findings.claim: GDD 2.3.7 and 4.5 risk 2: the value curve and the risk curve rise together, each band up is disproportionately hotter to return from, and the return leg must get strictly harder with altitude.
findings.measured: Flown, it inverts. Cheapest ablation by band at equal load: empty 4.1 (suborbital) / 3.6 (low) / 3.2 (high); half hold 6.8 / 5.9 / 5.2; full hold 10.0 / 8.7 / 7.7. Peak heat follows: 98 / 93 / 89 at full hold. Returning from the high band is 23% cheaper in plate and 9 points cooler than returning from suborbital, in every load case. Mass still works as designed — full hold costs 2.4x the plate of empty at high (7.7 vs 3.2) — so the greed axis holds while the altitude axis runs backwards. In the grid difficulty_rises_with_band is satisfied by only 38.6% of worlds, the second-rarest target after unstaged_pass_survivable, and the Researcher's own note predicted this: band entry speeds spread only 864 -> 954 m/s, giving high just 1.35x the flux of suborbital before any other effect.

findings.claim: GDD 2.3.1: shallow unstaged passes are survivable because cargo damage only begins at 100% heat, and coarse braking is meant to happen before staging while thrust remains to reshape the periapsis.
findings.measured: unstaged_braking reports suborbital shallow_pass_peak_heat 407 against heat_capacity 100, survivable=false; low reads 93, survivable=true. The intended descent shape is therefore unavailable from the band the player starts in — the suborbital hull cooks at 4x capacity on the pass the GDD calls a feather. Across the grid unstaged_pass_survivable is the rarest target of the eight at 13.0%, and the top-scoring worlds split on it: every config that buys strong skimming loses it (unstaged_peak_heat 339-439) and every config that keeps it has near-flat skim multipliers (0.958-0.987). The two rules are in tension across the whole space, not just at these values.

findings.claim: landing.descent_speed_full_hold_ms 4.18 is described as 'near the 5 m/s line and under it, which is what makes the Parachute a purchase rather than a formality', with Storage tiers buying a hard landing that the matching Parachute tier buys back.
findings.measured: Measured touchdown is 2.96 m/s empty, 3.54 half hold, 4.04 full hold — identical across all three bands, and soft_landing=true in all nine descents. The full-hold figure is 4.04 against the claimed 4.18, and it sits 19% under the 5 m/s line rather than against it. The sweep also flags that landing.parachute_area_m2 is absent from the params, so the model solved for the 610.5 m2 that reproduces the 4.18 claim — the measured speeds are anchored to the crew's own assertion rather than independent of it, and the params should state the area.

findings.claim: The params' ablation model assumes skims meaningfully bleed speed; the Researcher's baseline computes beta 267-533 kg/m2 staged from assumed masses of 1400/2800 kg.
findings.measured: Flown beta is 228.6 kg/m2 staged and 685.7 unstaged, a 3.0x staging benefit against the baseline's claimed 4.3x. Staged beta above ~200 is why a skim removes so little: the grid's only configs with strong skim multipliers (0.262-0.363) run beta 44.4, below the ~50 kg/m2 floor where first contact removes the whole orbit. The usable window between 'skim does nothing' and 'skim ends the orbit' is narrow in this world's geometry, and reference_area_m2 3.5 with dry_mass_kg 1200 puts the ship at the wrong end of it.

proposed_changes.reason: Ascent crashes at all three bands with zero fuel remaining, so raise the tank first — this takes base delta-v from 1666 to 4000*ln(2300/1200) = 2604 m/s, enough for the ~1350 m/s suborbital circularisation with real margin, at the cost of making fuel_tank t1 a smaller upgrade that should be repriced downward.

With the heavier tank, launch TWR at 4.0 m/s^2 falls to 16000/9200 = 1.74 and gravity losses eat the added delta-v; 26000 N restores TWR to 2.8 and lets the ship reach orbit at all, at the cost of a shorter burn time that fuel_burn_kgs must track.

Holds exhaust velocity at 26000/6.5 = 4000 m/s so the thrust increase buys acceleration and not free delta-v — the coupling the economy notes flagged as inexpressible in the upgrade schema, applied at base.

Every flown descent peaks at 64-98 and survives at base gear, so no band gates on a shield upgrade; 72 puts suborbital empty (70) just under the line, suborbital full (98) and low full (93) over it, restoring the upgrade ladder the params claim — at the cost of making an early full-hold suborbital run genuinely dangerous, which is the intended pillar.

The flown curve has cheapest_pass_count 1 in all nine descents with no interior minimum, so the asserted optimum is a claim the simulator contradicts; state the measured value until the ablation model or the skim strength changes, at the cost of admitting the 2-4 pass rule is not currently met.

GDD 4.5 risk 1's named fallback is a flat per-pass cost with a hard pass cap rather than a hunted U-curve; cutting the fixed toll to 0.2 makes the second pass cost 0.2 instead of 1.6-3.6 points of plate, so multi-pass stops being strictly punished — it does not by itself create an optimum, because the skim's 2.9-5.6% heat saving cannot outrun any toll at a cubic exponent.

Staged beta 228.6 is why skims remove almost nothing; 6.5 m2 at Cd_shield 1.5 drops staged beta to roughly 123 kg/m2 — a 1.9x stronger skim, still well clear of the ~50 floor where first contact eats the orbit — at the cost of a hotter, shorter committed entry and a re-check of the unstaged hull, which shares the reference area.

Reports the flown peak heat ordering (98 / 93 / 89 at full hold) instead of the shallowest-entry ordering, so the params stop asserting a band difficulty ramp the simulator inverts; it costs the GDD 2.3.7 claim, which should be carried by band-gated ablation rates as 4.5 risk 2 already names.
The flown figure is 4.04 m/s across all three bands; adopting it costs nothing and removes a claim the sweep measured directly.

The simulator had to solve for this from descent_speed_full_hold_ms because the params do not state it, which makes every measured touchdown speed partly circular; stating it makes the chute an independent input.

confidence_notes: The ascent failures are the least trustworthy result in the set and the most consequential. All three read the same way — crashed, zero fuel, zero margin — which is the signature of either a genuine delta-v shortfall or a simulator ascent guidance that flies one fixed profile badly. The economy agent's rocket-equation arithmetic (1666 m/s against a ~1350 m/s requirement) says the margin is thin but not absent. My proposed tank and thrust changes are sized to survive either explanation, but if the ascent model is at fault they overshoot and fuel_tank t1 becomes nearly pointless. Fly one ascent by hand before spending 480 kg of tank on it.

descent_speed_full_hold_ms is not an independent measurement. The sweep states it inferred parachute_area_m2 = 610.5 by solving for the crew's own 4.18 m/s claim, so the measured 4.04 m/s tests internal consistency of the mass scaling, not the chute. Treat the full_hold_lands_soft finding as low-confidence until the area is authored.

The difficulty_falls_with_altitude finding is robust to the simulator's limits — it appears in all nine descents, in both plate cost and peak heat, and the Researcher independently predicted it from entry speeds alone (864/906/954 m/s giving only 1.35x flux spread). But the flown inversion is larger than entry speed can explain, and I believe the cause is that the descent controller picks a deeper braking altitude from higher orbits (45030 m at high full hold versus 51295 m at suborbital), which brakes earlier and cooler. That is a pilot policy, not a physical law, and a human flying a shallow high-band entry would get a hotter one. The design conclusion stands; the exact magnitudes do not.

The simulator is a point mass with a perfect pilot. It has no attitude error, so GDD 2.3.1's cosine off-retrograde penalty is untested and reentry.off_retrograde_penalty 1 is an unflown number. It has no debris collisions, no EVA, and no tether physics — every claim in the params about magnet shear, tether slots, jetpack handling and stow costs is unmeasured by this sweep and I make no finding on any of it. It also cannot say whether a descent with no reason to skim feels boring, which is exactly the judgement GDD 3.3 checkpoint 3 reserves for the human.

My reference_area_m2 proposal is the one change I am least able to bound. The sweep shows beta is the controlling quantity for whether skimming exists, and shows the working window is narrow (44.4 gives real skims, 228.6 gives none), but it never flew an intermediate beta on this planet — the 44.4 configs are all 60 km worlds. 123 kg/m2 is interpolation, not measurement, and it should be swept before it is committed.

unstaged_pass_survivable at 13.0% across 324 worlds is the strongest evidence in either sweep that a GDD rule is unachievable rather than untuned, and it is in direct tension with skimming strength: in the top-12 list, every world with a skim multiplier below 0.4 has unstaged peak heat above 339. If the crew wants both, the honest move is 2.3.1's own structure — let staging change drag area and shield exposure independently, rather than tuning one number to satisfy both.
